source_binding.mechanism: Recovery-Block-style sequential alternates with an acceptance test, plus role-local authority generations for stale-completion rejection

public_sources.claim_used: Randell's 1975 work introduced recovery blocks as a software fault-tolerance structure for error detection and recovery.
The earlier recovery-block program structure includes automatic preservation of restart information for recovery from software errors.
Recovery blocks checkpoint state, evaluate a primary/alternate against a common acceptance test, try alternatives sequentially after rejection, and fail when no version passes.

source_binding.literal_external_runtime_reason: No external recovery-block runtime, hosted runner, cloud service, SDK, or user execution is required. Public sources supply only the alternate/acceptance/failure semantics.
source_binding.chat_native_reduction: Treat QUARANTINED_NO_AUTHORITY as the restart point, evaluate predeclared alternates C then D against the same role-local acceptance gates, preserve all evidence as immutable artifacts rather than destructive rollback, and use authority_epoch to reject delayed stale completions.

G9.evidence: Completions from epochs <=22 cannot mutate authority after D promotion.

G12.evidence: Accepted reduction uses recurring Chat reasoning and lightweight repository transport only; no richer/protected/manual execution, finite optional monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental monetary cost.

scope_limit: Constructed role-local fixed trace only. This does not show recovery blocks are sufficient for arbitrary common-mode acceptance-test faults or production fault tolerance.
unresolved_child: The common acceptance test can itself be systematically wrong; a later leaf should test acceptance-checker common-mode failure rather than assume the checker is authoritative.

quota_cost_assessment.repository_transport_note: Repository API is lightweight transport only; rate limits are checkpoint/retryable and are not used as compute.
